title: (Obj) for the constructible cocone
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $X$ a scheme whose underlying topological space is Noetherian. The
constructible cocone ([def-sfb-constructible-cocone]) satisfies (Obj) of
[sk-def-sfb-filtered-two-colimit]: every $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)$ is isomorphic to
$T_{E,\Qlb}K_E$ for some finite extension $E$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Qlb$ and some
$K_E\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$.

proof.text: Use $E_X=p_X^*C(-,E)$ and $\QbarX=p_X^*\underline{\Qlb}$, where the latter sections have image in one finite subfield. These are exactly $E_X^c,\Omega_X^c$ of the cited condensed-module definition: the pullback functors agree by their formulas. The cited local-presentation definitions both say locally a cokernel of finite free modules on each stratum. Thus their bounded constructible full subcategories agree. Put $\mathcal C_E=D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,E)$ and $\mathcal D=D(\Mod_{\QbarX})$.

source.place: Modules and Complexes paragraphs; unit proof (3), finite sheaf descent followed by Postnikov induction

proof.text: The finite-model API makes each $\mathcal C_E$ triangulated, using topological Noetherianity. Flat coefficient calculus makes scalar extension exact and termwise on derived categories. Therefore the cocone, with vertex included in $\mathcal D$, has triangulated functors $\Phi_E:\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal D$ and the same transition comparisons; the source inclusions are exact by the triangulated-subcategory definition.

source.place: Modules and Complexes paragraphs; unit proof (3), finite sheaf descent followed by Postnikov induction

proof.text: Put $P(Y)\iff\exists E,\ \exists K_E\in\mathcal C_E,\ Y\cong\Phi_E(K_E)$. The field index is nonempty. Fullness of $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Qlb)\subset\mathcal D$ lets Hom-surjectivity lift every ambient arrow between images to a common stage, with the specified comparisons. The directed-triangulated-image lemma gives that $P$ is triangulated. Composing witnessing isomorphisms makes $P$ isomorphism-closed.

source.place: Modules and Complexes paragraphs; unit proof (3), finite sheaf descent followed by Postnikov induction

proof.text: Finite-presentation descent gives, for every constructible $\QbarX$-module $M$, a constructible $E_X$-module $M_E$ with $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}M_E\cong M$. Its single complex is bounded constructible: $H^0=M_E$, all other cohomology is zero, with presentation $0\to0\to0$. Exact-functor single-complex compatibility and flat coefficient calculus give $\Phi_E(M_E[0])\cong M[0]$. Hence $P(M[0])$.

source.place: Modules and Complexes paragraphs; unit proof (3), finite sheaf descent followed by Postnikov induction

proof.text: Apply finite truncation devissage [lem-sfb-dc-module-devissage] to $\mathcal R=\QbarX$ and $P$: step 3 supplies triangulation and isomorphism closure, and step 4 supplies all constructible degree-zero objects. It gives $P(K)$ for every bounded constructible $K$.

source.place: Modules and Complexes paragraphs; unit proof (3), finite sheaf descent followed by Postnikov induction

proof.text: Unpack $P(K)$. Both $K$ and $\Phi_E(K_E)$ lie in the full cocone vertex, so the ambient isomorphism and its inverse are vertex morphisms. They exhibit exactly (Obj) for the specified cocone.
